page: Google Cloud Platform t2d-standard-8 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture. Powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor, the instance provides 8 dedicated physical cores mapped directly to 8 vCPUs with a single thread per core, backed by 32 MB of L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 32.0 GB, establishing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The instance includes no attached local storage and contains no discrete GPU hardware.

Benchmark results show competitive single-threaded capabilities alongside stable multi-core throughput. Stress-ng single-core performance reached 2688.09, ranking in the top 25 percent of tested systems, while multi-core stress-ng reached 21511.57. Memory throughput achieves 95.12 GB/sec for large uncached reads and 51.75 GB/sec for large block writes. Geekbench tests recorded a single-core score of 1455.0 and a multi-core score of 7817.0, with PassMark CPU overall scoring 16769.54 and database operations measured at 6859.59.

Because the configuration uses fully dedicated physical cores rather than simultaneous multithreading threads, it provides consistent CPU execution without hyperthread contention. This core model yields reliable efficiency for workloads that require predictable per-core latency. The absence of integrated local NVMe storage requires external persistent disks for stateful applications, which influences architecture choices.

The balance of 8 dedicated cores and 32 GB of memory makes t2d-standard-8 suitable for standard application backends, container orchestration nodes, static web serving, intermediate database hosting, and CI/CD build environments.
description: Google Cloud Platform t2d-standard-8 is a general-purpose instance featuring 8 vCPUs and 32.0 GB of memory on the x86_64 architecture. Equipped with an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor, it provisions 8 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading, supported by 32 MB of L3 cache. It lacks local storage and GPU hardware, depending on networked block storage for persistent data. In benchmark evaluations, the t2d-standard-8 delivered top-quartile single-core stress-ng execution alongside steady mid-tier multi-threaded and memory bandwidth metrics, including 95.12 GB/sec large-block uncached read speeds. The 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation and dedicated compute cores provide predictable compute throughput for web serving, microservices, continuous integration pipelines, and general relational database workloads.
